key_insight: ASCENT exposes gaps in LLMs’ stepwise diagnostic reasoning that standard medical question answering can miss, while targeted fine-tuning improves performance.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating how models revise diagnostic impressions as information accumulates better reflects clinical workflows, but does not establish readiness for patient care.
method: Built 3,078 clinician-annotated stepwise problems from MedQA-USMLE.
Organized vignettes into EMR-aligned findings, impressions, and supporting rationales.
Evaluated models, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B and 32B, and tested robustness.
evidence_signal: ASCENT fine-tuning improved F1 over pre-trained and HuatuoGPT-o1 CoT-trained baselines, primarily through precision gains; even strong reasoning models showed substantial room for improvement.
watch_item: Errors can propagate across sequential diagnostic steps, and benchmark gains do not demonstrate real-world clinical safety or effectiveness.
paper_title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
